groups.text: It is currently 14 degrees and cloudy in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

Pakistan is moving to establish its first-ever Strategic Petroleum Reserves after escalating Middle East tensions and shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz exposed a fragile, just-in-time inventory model. Islamabad plans an initial 45-day emergency oil buffer, eventually aiming for 90 days, while inviting Saudi Arabia and Kuwait to maintain reserves at Gwadar Port. To fund this shift, Pakistan has requested a six point seven billion dollar deferred-payment oil facility from Saudi Arabia with a one percent interest rate. Meanwhile, in Cameroon, an investigation reveals that barely five percent of the country's gold production passes through legal channels, with billions in gold escaping via international airports. In unrelated news from the research community, some machine learning researchers are reporting concerns over noisy scores and AI-generated reviews within the ARR 2026 meta review process, specifically questioning how overall scores are rounded or adjusted by reviewers.

Violence is escalating across the Middle East following a series of strikes and counter-attacks. Iran's Revolutionary Guards claim to have destroyed a US early-warning radar system in Kuwait, where plumes of black smoke were seen over the town of Mangaf. In Bahrain, air raid sirens triggered as explosions were heard over the capital city of Manama. Meanwhile, state media reports that at least one person was killed and several others wounded during overnight US strikes southwest of Tabriz in northwestern Iran. In the United States, hundreds of people rallied in Houston on Sunday to demand justice for Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, a fifty-two-year-old Mexican national shot dead by an ICE agent on July seventh. Protesters marched from Ervan Chew Park and briefly shut down a bridge on Dunlavy Street. Separately, the BBC has released a new "Who am I?" game challenging fans to identify a World Cup star.

The war between the United States, Israel, and Iran is reshaping security in the Arab world, forcing Gulf states to cooperate against shared threats like drone attacks on energy infrastructure. This tension was highlighted when President Donald Trump briefly proposed a twenty percent fee on ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz before withdrawing the idea after talks with Gulf nations. Politologist Hanna Voß notes that while these states are aligning for security, deep political rivalries remain and prevent a unified foreign policy. Meanwhile, in Kenya, founder Hemal Doshil is targeting a different kind of fragmentation within the construction supply chain. His startup, Eyby, has launched a digital marketplace to connect manufacturers, distributors, and buyers on one platform. Though still in private beta, the service already facilitates five million dollars in monthly gross merchandise value by replacing manual quotation processes with a centralized digital catalog.

San Francisco City Attorney David Chiu is demanding that Apple and Google remove thirteen apps from their stores capable of generating non-consensual sexual deepfakes. Eight of these "nudify" apps are on the App Store and five are on the Play Store, despite both companies claiming their platforms are safe spaces that prohibit pornography and harassment. This misuse of AI contrasts with a different kind of fraud in India, where the Securities and Exchange Board of India is warning listed companies about the "Boss Scam." In these attacks, fraudsters use voice cloning and deepfakes to impersonate senior executives and trick finance teams into transferring funds. Meanwhile, physical destruction continues in Ukraine, where Russian missiles struck a warehouse belonging to the Knigolav publishing house. The attack destroyed 250,000 books, though no employees were injured in the strike.

Violence erupted during protests across three continents this week. In New Delhi, police baton-charged thousands of supporters of the youth-led cockroach movement as they attempted to march on parliament on Monday. The unrest follows the forced hospitalization of activist Sonam Wangchuk and represents a significant public challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's third term. Meanwhile, in Aurora, Colorado, an employee of the GEO Group shot 21-year-old Emma Landis in the foot during a protest outside an ICE processing center on Thursday night. Police say Brandon Booth used a personal firearm after protesters blocked his entrance to the facility while shouting about tuberculosis outbreaks and poor conditions inside the center. Shifting to Southeast Asia, political tensions are mounting ahead of the August 1 state polls in Negeri Sembilan. Following a poor showing for Pakatan Harapan in Johor, this upcoming election is seen as a bellwether for the federal government's stability before the 2028 national polls.

Tensions are escalating in the Middle East as Donald Trump confirms the United States has struck Iranian command centers and communication networks to avenge killed American soldiers. In response, the Kuwaiti army reports new Iranian drone attacks following claims from the Revolutionary Guards that they hit U.S. targets in Kuwait. Meanwhile, air raid sirens sounded in Manama after explosions were heard in the Bahraini capital. This volatility contrasts with a different kind of crisis in Ukraine, where Russian forces launched over ten drone attacks on the Dnipropetrovsk region, damaging a market and a logistics warehouse. Shifting to environmental concerns, a new study warns that critical shark and ray habitats in India remain unprotected despite the country being the world's second-largest shark-fishing nation. Researchers note that global abundance of these species has fallen by 71 percent since 1970, leaving over three-quarters of them threatened with extinction.

Attackers are already exploiting two newly patched WordPress vulnerabilities known as WP2Shell. These flaws, tracked as CVE-2026-60137 and CVE-2026-63030, allow anonymous users to achieve remote code execution on affected sites. To combat the threat, WordPress has enabled forced updates for versions 6.9.0 through 7.0.1, while Cloudflare rolled out detection rules. In a different sector of consumer costs, Apple is raising prices for AppleCare+ and Apple Music, citing higher licensing costs. Individual plans now cost 11.99 euros per month, though they remain cheaper than Spotify's individual premium rate. Meanwhile, in Pakistan, the start of the sugarcane crushing season has reignited a recurring conflict over pricing. Farmers are demanding higher prices to offset production costs, while sugar mills argue such increases make the business unviable. This tension highlights a broader struggle between treating the crop as a pricing problem versus a productivity challenge.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will bring showers with temperatures between 16 and 21 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.

On your calendar today: personal calendar: all day: Sommerferien 2026 Berlin, at 09:00, FW: AP2 meeting at Microsoft Teams Meeting, at 14:00, Monthly Engineering All Hands, at 18:45, BLISS Reading Group at Merantix AI Campus, and at 19:00, AI Enthusiasts at c-base mainhall, AI Meetup at c-base, and ️ Twerchhau.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
